text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
British meteorologist, SIR CHARLES TODD, who developed Australia's overland telegraph line, was born in 1826.

Cartoonist with the Sydney Bulletin magazine, LIVINGSTON HOPKINS, known as "HOP", was born in the United States in 1846. Despite HIS 19,000 works of wit and satire, Australian artist NORMAN LINDSAY described HOPKINS as "quite humourless ... an inflexible autocrat."
French fashion designer, PIERRE CARDIN, was born in 1922.
Australian author and film producer, ROBERT RAYMOND, was born in 1922.

'Beatles' drummer, RINGO STARR, (RICHARD STARKEY) was born in 1940. Before joining JOHN, PAUL and GEORGE, RINGO played with the 'Eddie Clayton Skiffle Group' and 'Rory Storm and the Hurricanes'. RINGO began a solo career after the 'Beatles' split. His hits included "It Don't Come Easy " (1971), "Back Off Boogaloo" (1972), You're Sixteen" (1973), and "Only You" (1974).
Actress CARMEN DUNCAN was born in the northern New South Wales town of Lismore in 1942.
American actress SHELLY LONG was born in 1949. She appeared in the long-running television series "Cheers" and recently took the role of CAROL in the Brady Bunch movie.
United States singer with the 'Village People', DAVID HODO, was born in 1950.
British singer and guitarist, CLIVE JACKSON, from 'Doctor and the Medics' was born in 1962. They had a hit in 1986 with "Spirit in the Sky."
** EVENTS **
1307 : English King EDWARD I, conqueror of the Welsh,
died on his way to Scotland to fight ROBERT the BRUCE.
1815 : Following NAPOLEON's defeat at Waterloo on June
18, the victorious allies marched into Paris.
1853 : Japan opened up to trade after 250 years of

isolation. United States Naval officer Commodore MATTHEW PERRY persuaded the Shogun to reverse a decision made in 1639 after Japan expelled the Spanish and Portuguese. Backed by armed ships in Edo Harbour, PERRY convinced the Shogun that the Japanese should treat shipwrecked sailors with more consideration and that American vessels should be allowed to trade in at least one port.
1930 : Creator of sleuth Sherlock Holmes and his sidekick
Dr Watson, SIR ARTHUR CONAN DOYLE, died at the age of 71.
1940 : Brisbane's Story Bridge was opened. It was
Australia's second longest span bridge.
1941 : American troops moved into Iceland to deter any
attack by Nazis. President FRANKLIN D. ROOOSEVELT ordered the occupation to release British troops. Although the United States was not officially at war with Germany the country was committed
to the Allied cause.
1950 : The first airshow was held at Farnborough in
Surrey, England.
1960 : One of Australia's most sensational kidnapping

cases began in Sydney. The kidnapper of eight-year-old GRAEME THORNE demanded 25,000 pounds from his parents who had just won 100,000 pounds in a lottery. The boy was picked up in a Bondi street. It was the first case of its kind in Australia. Police believed the kidnappers had watched the boy's movements for

about a week before the abduction. Despite an extensive manhunt and a televised plea by his parents, the boy was murdered and his body found in a cave at Seaforth just over a month later. In the wake of the case, Federal Parliament introduced a bill for kidnappers to be whipped and jailed for life. STEPHEN LESLIE BRADLEY was extraditied from Colombo to stand trial. Cries of "feed him to the sharks" and cheers filled the court as BRADLEY was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
1970 : The founder of Penquin publishing, SIR ALLEN LANE,
died. He was the first publisher to promote the paperback novel.
1982 : QUEEN ELIZABETH woke to find an intruder sitting

on her bed in the royal suite in Buckingham Palace. 30 year-old MICHAEL FAGAN was drinking from a bottle of wine that he'd taken from the QUEEN's cellar, and he wanted a chat. It wasn't until FAGAN asked for a cigarette that the QUEEN was able to summon help. FAGAN was charged with theft of wine while trespassing. The incident highlighted security problems at the palace.
1985 : Germany's BORIS BECKER, at 17, became the youngest

player ever to win the Wimbledon men's singles title. He defeated South African KEVIN CURREN 6-3, 6-7, 7-6, 6-4, to also become the first German and first unseeded player to take the tennis crown. During his attempt at the title the previous year, BECKER left the tournament in a wheelchair, after injuring himself in a 3rd-round match.
1986 : The Malaysian Government executed two Australians,
KEVIN JONH BARLOW and BRIAN GEOFFREY CHAMBERS, for drug trafficking. BARLOW, 28, and CHAMBERS, 29, were the first westerners to be hanged under the country's anti-narcotic laws.
1988 : An eleven-year-old American boy pilot took-off
from San Diego, bound for Paris.
